 LIVE Updated 35 mins ago Anthropic IPO live: Anthropic stock drops after first day of trading
 Daniel Howley · Technology Editor Updated Fri, November 20, 2026 at 2:00 PM EST 1 min read ANT -10.67% 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) stock dropped about 9% in early trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Not helping sentiment: the broader market plunged on Anthropic's well-received IPO day and remains under pressure today. 
 Anthropic made a monster debut on Wall Street Thursday, with shares opening at $111.50 a little before noon ET, a 34% premium to the $83 IPO price. 
 But the AI company's stock couldn't hold on to its early gains. The stock began trading just after 11:30 a.m. ET, at $111.50 per share, but pared those gains throughout the afternoon, ending at $97.17. 
 That closing price gave Anthropic a market capitalization of about $1.28 trillion, or roughly $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis. 
 CEO Dario Amodei and president Daniela Amodei were at the Nasdaq in Times Square to ring the opening bell ahead of the first trade on Thursday, with Dario saying that safety will be key to how AI is developed and deployed. 
 Daniela Amodei, meanwhile, addressed concerns about AI growth, saying, "To anyone watching who is uneasy about AI or unsure what it will mean for you. This technology needs you. Not your trust, not your use, but your voice." 
 Anthropic, which Yahoo Finance named its Company of the Year for 2026 , reported in its most recent amended S-1 that its third-quarter revenue climbed to $17 billion, a 12x year over year increase. 
 Now the market will determine how that risk factors into the company's future prospects.

 Today at 6:13 PM UTC Ben Werschkul 'I have a lot of respect for Dario': Trump weighs in on Anthropic IPO
 President Trump touted Anthropic's ( ANT ) "very successful launch" in brief comments at the White House during a press conference Friday to discuss his recent trip to Asia. 
 "I have a lot of respect for Dario," the president added of CEO Dario Amodei, noting the record size of the IPO. 
 The comments also came amid another defense of data centers from the president and America's position on artificial intelligence, with the president saying of China: "We are leading, and they are second." 
 The president also unveiled new plans during Friday's press conference to deny tech companies the ability to build data centers outside the United States "because China will take all of them," saying tech giants would face unspecified tax penalties if they don't comply. 
 Today at 5:54 PM UTC Catherine Brock Anthropic stock slips after record IPO. Should you hold, sell, or buy more?
 Anthropic ( ANT ) began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday, Nov. 19, after setting an IPO price of $83 per share. The first trade at $111.50, amid troubled market conditions, showed optimism for the AI company's future. The stock closed the day at $97.17 and has since weakened, dropping 9% in early trading on Friday. 
 If an IPO stock is sliding, you generally shouldn't sell on price alone. This guide covers when selling or holding makes sense, what to watch for next, and the tax rules for losses. 
 Today at 4:04 PM UTC Ines Ferré Anthropic stock extends losses, falls 12%
 Anthropic ( ANT ) stock extended losses, dropping as much as 12% on Friday amid an overall AI trade meltdown. 
 Shares of the AI developer sank on their first full day of trading following the record-breaking IPO. 
 Nearly every corner of the AI trade was under pressure on Friday, with semiconductor stock leading the way lower. 
 Anthropic was trading near $85 per share as of 11 a.m. ET on Friday, still above its IPO price of $83. The stock, however, is down sharply from its opening price of $111.50 when it began trading on Thursday.

 Today at 3:10 PM UTC Brian Sozzi Anthropic just went public. Here's what SpaceX and Facebook IPOs tell us about where the stock goes next.
 History shows you may not want to get sucked into the excitement over Anthropic ( ANT ) now that it's past its much-hyped IPO. 
 The average maximum drawdown for major IPOs 12 months after their debuts, dating back to 2004, is a 55.4% drop, per data from Carson Group chief market strategist Ryan Detrick. 
 The award for the worst post-IPO decline goes to Circle ( CRCL ), with an 80.9% decline. The best is Mastercard ( MA ), with a 13.1% decline. 
 SpaceX's ( SPCX ) decline tallied 48.8%. 
 "Looking at previous major IPOs shows that a pop on Day 1 is common. But so is a massive correction at some point over the next year," Detrick said. 
 Shares of Anthropic dropped in early trading on Friday as investors booked profits after a frenetic first day of trading. Read more .

 Today at 2:41 PM UTC Yahoo Finance Anthropic stock open down 9%
 A day after its record-breaking debut, Anthropic shares fell 9% from a closing price of $97, though they remain above their IPO price of $83. After a big pop on its IPO day, Anthropic faces a test in the markets to see whether it can keep the momentum going. 
 Today at 2:00 PM UTC Jared Blikre Anthropic's IPO buyers made $14 billion on day one, second only to SpaceX
 Anthropic and SpaceX ended their IPO debuts with nearly the same pop. They just got there from opposite directions. 
 Anthropic ( ANT ) closed its first day of trading Thursday at $97.17, 17% above its $83 IPO price. SpaceX ( SPCX ) closed its June debut at $160.95, up 19%. 
 That left Anthropic worth about $1.27 trillion at the close, based on the 13.09 billion implied shares outstanding on its Yahoo Finance quote page. That's roughly 60% of the $2.1 trillion SpaceX fetched after its first day, according to the Wall Street Journal. Counting options and other stock awards, the fully diluted figure is closer to $1.6 trillion. 
 The paths are where they split. SpaceX's first trade came in just 11% above its IPO price, and the stock climbed from there. Anthropic opened with a $12 billion trade at $111.50, 34% above its IPO price. Then it cooled off for the rest of the day. 
 Read more . 
 Today at 1:30 PM UTC Hamza Shaban Anthropic's IPO ties the fate of the US economy closer to AI
 Anthropic's historic IPO is notable not just for its size , but also for what it says — and will say — about the makeup of the stock market and the outsized influence of its largest players. 
 The top 10 biggest companies make up close to 40% of the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ). A bad day for tech means a bad day for the market. And now that Anthropic has joined the trillion-dollar ticker club — though it won't join the S&P 500 anytime soon — Wall Street's fate is tightly bound to another huge tech company, which also happens to be an AI lab without a long track record of financial stability. 
 The top-heavy nature of the S&P 500 means the benchmark index is less diverse than it looks. Sure, investors are buying into a basket of hundreds of names. But since the tickers with the largest market caps get the highest proportional weights, a handful of names can move the entire index. 
 That's how you can get such different performances from the equal-weighted S&P 500 ( ^SPXEW ) index (up 11% so far this year) versus the standard, market-weighted version (up 6%). Read more . 
 Today at 12:48 PM UTC Jared Blikre Anthropic's IPO winners and losers, from Ashton Kutcher to Sam Bankman-Fried
 Ashton Kutcher and Sam Bankman-Fried both bet early on Anthropic. Only one is celebrating its public market debut. 
 Bankman-Fried's FTX put $500 million into Anthropic ( ANT ) in 2021 for about 14% of the AI lab. After FTX collapsed, the estate sold the stake in 2024 for about $1.3 billion. Among the buyers was Jane Street, the trading firm where Bankman-Fried got his start. 
 That stake was worth more than $40 billion at Anthropic's first-day close of $97.17 — even after the stock opened at $111.50 , 34% above its $83 IPO price, and gave back part of the pop. Bankman-Fried, who is serving a 25-year sentence, told the New York Times from prison that he tries not to dwell on it. "There's no point in obsessing over regrets," he said. "But it's certainly something that I've spent, despite that, a fair bit of time thinking through." 
 Kutcher, meanwhile, had a different response : "Kind of cool," the actor said of the IPO on X. Sound Ventures, the firm he co-founded with Madonna's manager Guy Oseary, first backed Anthropic in 2023. Its $435 million turned into about $6 billion by the close, with some outlets reporting that the debut could make Kutcher a billionaire , despite his recent exit from the firm . NBA star Tristan Thompson is another celebrity backer, and he isn't selling . 
 Anthropic's seven co-founders were worth about $163 billion combined at the close, or more than $23 billion apiece, by Yahoo Finance calculations. They were the only insiders selling in the IPO, at about $280 million each. 
 The seven have pledged to give away 80% of their stock. That's about $130 billion at the close, more than the Gates Foundation's entire $92 billion endowment. The filing calls the pledges "voluntary, revocable," and the seven keep 50.1% of the vote either way. 
 Employees did fine as well. Their options and restricted stock were worth about $270 billion at the close. The average option costs just $2.91 a share to exercise, on a stock that closed at $97.17. 
 And then there's Big Tech. Read more . 
 Today at 12:00 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Anthropic’s IPO could deliver $156 billion to charity
 TechCrunch breaks down how Anthropic's IPO could not only make its employees and founders generationally wealthy but also provide a windfall to charitable causes: 
 As you might expect from a company whose leadership emerged from the world of effective altruism (EA), Anthropic has multiple different avenues for cash raised in its market debut to be directed to philanthropy. 
 First, the company's Public Benefit Fund, or PBF (analogous to OpenAI's foundation), was allotted 5% of the company's shares, almost 850 million. At the current trading price of about $95, that will leave it with an endowment of $80 billion. And if the company continues its astonishing growth rate, Anthropic could add further 2% increases every time the company's valuation grows more than 50% over the IPO price of $83, or about $124.50 per share for the next threshold. 
 The PBF's money will be focused on research and activities related to increasing the benefit of artificial intelligence to humanity. The first commitment of the PBF was $200 million to study the impact of AI on workers; Anthropic has said it will consider donations to philanthropic organizations or "direct distributions to specific populations" — perhaps a hint of future UBI plans. 
 Anthropic also donated $50 million to the city of San Francisco last week. A company spokesperson tells TechCrunch the donation did not come from the PBF.

 Today at 10:00 AM UTC Claire Boston AI wealth is already changing San Francisco's housing market
 Thursday's blockbuster Anthropic ( ANT ) initial public offering created thousands of new millionaires, and that wealth is already transforming housing markets in San Francisco and the Bay Area.  
 Median down payment sizes are rising in Northern California communities with the most AI and tech employers, according to an analysis by Realtor.com, a trend that started just before AI began seeing mass adoption in 2023.  
 n three counties where AI companies are particularly concentrated — San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara — the median homebuyer now makes a 25% down payment, up from a median of 20%-21% from 2020 to 2022. In contrast, median down payments have held steady at 20% in nearby counties with fewer AI employers.  
 In the pricey Bay Area, boosting a down payment by 5 percentage points means ponying up serious cash. The median home in the region costs $1.33 million, meaning the difference between a 20% and a 25% down payment is more than $60,000.  
 "Even as rates eased, buyers in some major markets continued to put more money down, which is consistent with AI and tech wealth changing who is buying homes," Realtor.com senior economist Jiayi Xu said in a statement. 
 Today at 8:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Anthropic has a 17-fold revenue growth hurdle to tackle
 Bessemer Venture Partners' Byron Deeter points out that Anthropic's massive revenue growth so far creates a major challenge for the company in the coming quarters as it looks to maintain its momentum. 
 "They've basically [grown] 10X for the last two years, and achieving that level of growth typically is hard to see without customer concentration," Deeter said on Deirdre Bosa Live. 
 Bosa noted that Anthropic will need to increase revenue by approximately 17-fold in the next decade to deliver a return comparable to Big Tech companies like Apple, Alphabet, and Microsoft. 
 "You typically have an early adopter or two who've pulled forward the capability, but in the case of Anthropic, as they shared in the prospectus, it's fairly well distributed," Deeter noted. 
 Today at 6:00 AM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nasdaq president on how Anthropic could be fast-tracked into Nasdaq 100
 Anthropic stock ( ANT ) is on course to be fast-tracked into the Nasdaq-100 ( ^NDX ), giving the company exposure to a broader set of investors and retirement accounts. 
 Nasdaq created a new rule this year, ahead of the SpaceX ( SPCX ) IPO, to allow megacap companies that have recently debuted to be added to the index more quickly. The top 40 non-financial companies by market capitalization are eligible for the sped-up process. 
 "After the seventh business day of trading, we will evaluate Anthropic, and if they're in that top 40, which clearly it looks like they will be, they will go into the index," Nasdaq president Nelson Griggs told Yahoo Finance's Pras Subramanian (see video below). 
 Anthropic is also eligible because it listed its shares on the Nasdaq. If Anthropic makes the cut, as Griggs expects, then it will be considered during the index's yearly reconstitution in December. 
 "The average return [for the Nasdaq-100] over the last 20 years is upwards of 16% versus the S&P at 11%," Griggs said of the index's performance. "It really is the companies that are redefining the future of the world."

 Anthropic frames its work around AI safety. Yahoo Finance anchors discuss. 
 Today at 4:00 AM UTC Yahoo Finance Anthropic IPO heightens Washington’s tech scrutiny
 Semafor reports : 
 Anthropic's blockbuster IPO is heightening Washington's scrutiny of the tech sector as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress armed with a long list of AI leaders to investigate. 
 Already, lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have raised concerns over the risks, including the potential for advanced AI models to be abused and the additional volatility such IPOs could introduce into the financial system. 
 A bipartisan Senate quartet introduced legislation on Thursday that would require publicly traded companies to disclose more information about AI. 
 "Wall Street shouldn't be cashing in on a company that could turn out to be a ticking time bomb," Rep. Pramila Jayapal, D-Wash., said. "Going public cements a broken business model and rewards its reckless pace." 
 The Senate Banking Committee's top Democrat, Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, called for quick congressional action on "safeguards on advanced AI development." 
 Outside groups are using the IPO as an opportunity to push for more stringent controls, too.

 Today at 2:00 AM UTC Yahia Barakah How does Anthropic make money? Inside the business of AI.
 AI companies make money mostly through subscriptions and model usage, and some also sell ads. 
 According to the IPO filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Anthropic, the creator of Claude, earned $33.24 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026. About 79% of that came from usage fees paid by developers and businesses, and 21% came from subscriptions. Revenue is not profit: Anthropic reported a $1.26 billion operating loss over the same nine-month period, driven largely by high computing costs. 
 Anthropic (ANT) , which began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT, opened at $111.50 per share on Nov. 19. The company's IPO filing gives us a rare look at how an AI company makes money and where that money goes. 
 If you're considering investing in Anthropic or other AI companies, it's worth understanding how these companies earn money and what they spend it on. Read more .
